title: From Humble Beginnings
body:
I got my first computer back in 2001. My aunt came over from the Netherlands, and brought a laptop with her. A small Pentium 2 Dell machine. To me, it looked like an absolute spaceship. The first gaming disc I got was a pirated compilation of games for Sega Genesis. 256 of them to be exact. I spent hours upon hours mastering each and every one of those. Those were my first steps into the world of gaming.

As time went on, I began to yearn for other gaming experiences. My Pentium 2 wasn't up to the task of delivering novel gaming experiences, so I visited my friends who had modern computers, and just sat back and watched them play. I was mesmerized. Diablo, Halo, Warcraft 3. I would go back home, open my notebook, and just draw what I could remember from the games I just watched. Those little doodles were my little portal to happiness.

I got a new computer when I was 8. It was a Pentium 4. Way better than the little laptop I had before, but still not good enough to play anything that was new at the time. Games were expensive, so I had to resort to buying pirated discs on the flea market. I did not know a single person that owned a single original video game. Still, I was happy - I got to play Fallout, Baldur's Gate, Simpsons: Hit & Run, and many others that have evaporated from my mind in the mean time.

My dad bought a LCD TV in 2009, in preparation for the 2010 World Cup. The TV was amazing for that time, and I remember he was saving up to buy it for quite some time. Unexpectedly, the TV came with a gift - a free PS2 slim. PS3 was all the rage at the time, but I vividly remember feeling ecstatic - I was about to unbox my first console. I had it modded, and I was buying one game a month from my flea market dealer. The assortment of games he was offering was slim, but I took what I could find. And I loved every second of it.

My collection officially started in August 2012. My aunt, the very same one that brought me my first computer, brought some old consoles from her boys - a PSP and a DS, along with a couple of games. My cousins were already playing on their Vita/3DS/PS3, so she was pretty much saving the consoles from being thrown in the trash. One man's trash is, indeed, another man's treasure. I remember putting the games on the shelf, and thinking - "When I grow up, I want to have more of these". And, yeah, I absolutely manifested that into existence.

As time went on, I found my own footing and started buying the games myself. Putting away every penny I could, and buying games here and there whenever I had the opportunity. With each passing year I added new gems to my collection. Some were gifts from the people I care about, some were random finds in random stores, places, countries. Each one of them tells a different story, and I feel that story whenever I take one of the cases in my hands. I don't have the time to play games as I used to, but I do my best. The fire that video games light inside me does not need rekindling, because it's been burning ever since I booted up that raggedy old Pentium 2. 

And long may it burn.
